jobs.company: The Pavilion at Camelback Senior Living
jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Job Description

The Executive Director is responsible for managing the day-to-day operations of the Community, achieving and maintaining maximum occupancy of the Community, achieving high resident/employee satisfaction, generating respect in the neighborhood for the Community, ensuring smooth operation of the Community and reaching the projected budget objectives for the company.

In This Position, Your Main Responsibilities Will Include

Ensure positive resident, family, and employee relations by responding promptly and appropriately to their needs, requests, concerns, and suggestions.
Perform marketing and sales activities including public relations efforts, prospective resident follow-up, and direct sales monitoring to ensure positive occupancy percentages.
Recruit, hire, train, motivate, and educate staff in all departments.
Operate the Community in a manner that will ensure company profitability by exceeding all community budget and census guidelines as set by the company.
Perform administrative duties including month-end reports. Timely and accurate completion of all daily, weekly, and monthly billings, and accounting and bookkeeping requirements (i.e., residents, A/R, A/P, payroll, collections, etc.)
Comply with all state and federal laws and regulations and all company rules regarding the operation of the Community.
Have a basic understanding and knowledge of Fair Housing Rules/Laws.

Qualifications

To be successful in this position, we believe that you need the following experiences, strengths, and skills:

Minimum of high school diploma. Bachelor’s degree preferred.
Assisted Living Administrator Certification/License required in Arizona, Missouri, New Mexico, Kansas, Colorado and Texas.
Must have at least seven years of experience in senior living or multifamily residential with three years’ experience in leadership role.
Must comply with all State and Federal mandated training and/or certification programs for the position of Executive Director.
Current state specific driver’s license and appropriate driving record.

Additional Information

If you join Spectrum as a full-time team member, your story will include eligibility for medical insurance, dental insurance, vision insurance, life insurance, and other voluntary insurance options. All part-time and full-time team members are eligible to participate in our 401(k), for paid time off, holiday pay, and discounts through Perk Spot.

Spectrum Retirement Communities strongly encourage all team members to be fully vaccinated against COVID-19, however, the vaccine is not a requirement to work with us.

Spectrum Retirement, LLC and all affiliates are Equal Opportunity Employers. We do not discriminate against employees or applicants on the basis of race, color, national origin, gender, sex, sexual orientation, pregnancy, gender identity or expression, disability, religion, age, genetic information, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law.

Spectrum Retirement, LLC also participates in the E-verify program through the Department of Homeland Security and the Social Security Administration.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Description

About the Wellness Equity Institute

The Wellness Equity Institute (WEI) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to reimagining the delivery of population, public, and community health services.

Operating At The Intersection Of Clinical Delivery, Public Health Systems Strengthening, And Community-based Implementation, WEI Focuses On Historically Marginalized And Underserved Communities, Including

People experiencing homelessness
Indigenous communities
Immigrant communities
Rural communities
BIPOC communities
LGBTQIA+ communities
Justice-impacted communities

Through specialized Technical Assistance, community health assessments, systems coordination, and innovative care models, including integrated community health centers that combine physical clinics with mobile street-medicine outreach, WEI works to dismantle systemic barriers and make health equity a standard of care.

WEI works in close alignment with the Wellness Equity Alliance (WEA) to build scalable, sustainable networks of care that meet people exactly where they are.

Position Summary

The Executive Director provides visionary and strategic leadership for the Wellness Equity Institute, guiding the organization's mission, governance, financial sustainability, and programmatic growth.

As WEI's chief executive, the Executive Director works in close partnership with the Board of Directors to establish strategic direction, strengthen organizational accountability, and ensure continued alignment with WEI's mission and values.

This is a part-time, 0.2 FTE leadership
opportunity designed for a seasoned executive who can drive high-impact strategic outcomes within a flexible, condensed time commitment.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership & Governance

Provide visionary leadership to advance WEI's mission of reshaping public and population health infrastructure.
Partner closely with the Board of Directors to strengthen governance, establish organizational benchmarks, and report transparently on progress toward strategic goals.
Lead strategic planning processes that support organizational growth and long-term sustainability.
Drive cross-sector collaborations connecting public health initiatives with healthcare networks, managed care plans, and municipal and public agencies.

Operational Oversight & Program Integration

Provide high-level oversight of the design and scaling of pilot programs, Technical Assistance frameworks, and Community Health Assessments.
Guide the integration of innovative care-delivery models, including brick-and-mortar clinics paired with mobile street-medicine outreach networks.
Ensure organizational adherence to clinical rigor, regulatory compliance, data security, and program evaluation standards.
Foster an organizational culture grounded in trauma-informed practices, cultural responsiveness, and collective care.
Delegate day-to-day operational management to senior staff while maintaining strategic accountability.

Financial Management & Fundraising

Serve as a principal steward of WEI's financial health, overseeing annual budgets and maintaining fiscal accountability to the Board of Directors.
Lead fund development strategy, including cultivating corporate partnerships, securing major philanthropic gifts, and expanding local, state, and federal grant opportunities.
Develop and guide sustainable operational and revenue models that support WEI's long-term impact.
Provide strategic oversight and input on major funding proposals and grant applications.

Advocacy, Communications & Community Relations

Serve as a primary external spokesperson for WEI, amplifying community voices and building public trust.
Advocate for inclusive public health policies and support educational initiatives addressing social determinants of health.
Leverage data and population health analytics generated by research teams to help influence systemic change in healthcare delivery.
Develop and maintain relationships with key stakeholders, including policymakers, funders, healthcare partners, and community leaders.

Team Leadership & Organizational Culture

Provide strategic guidance and support to senior staff responsible for day-to-day operations, programs, and clinical services.
Champion a low-ego, high-empathy leadership approach that supports multidisciplinary teams of clinicians, peer navigators, researchers, and administrative professionals.
Ensure organizational decisions reflect equity-centered values and community-driven priorities.

Requirements

Required Qualifications

Education

Master's degree in Public Health (MPH), Health Administration (MHA), Public Administration (MPA), Business Administration (MBA), or a related field.
A clinical doctoral degree such as an MD, DO, NP, or PhD is highly preferred.

Experience

7–10 years of progressive leadership experience within a nonprofit organization, public health agency, community health center/FQHC, or healthcare enterprise.
Demonstrated experience designing, implementing, or managing health programs serving unsheltered populations, historically marginalized communities, or rural populations.
Experience managing multimillion-dollar operational budgets.
Demonstrated success securing diversified funding through philanthropy, fee-for-service models, public grants, or similar funding sources.
Experience coordinating complex systems, breaking down organizational or structural silos, and mobilizing diverse stakeholder coalitions.

Preferred Skills & Capabilities

Exceptional public speaking, storytelling, and relationship-building abilities across diverse audiences, including community members, corporate boards, funders, and policymakers.
Familiarity with geographic information systems (GIS), population health tools, or data science applications in public health delivery.
Experience working with multi-ethnic, diverse, and underserved communities.
Demonstrated passion for innovative approaches to improving healthcare delivery and addressing systemic barriers.
Ability to operate effectively in a part-time, high-trust, outcomes-focused executive leadership role.

Work Arrangement

This position is remote in Southern California, with occasional travel for Board meetings, site visits, funder engagements, partnership events, or other key organizational activities.

The role is structured at approximately 0.2 FTE, or one day per week
, with an emphasis on strategic leadership, organizational outcomes, and executive-level accountability.
